title: A completely smooth reunion
promptMarkdown: In flat 1+1 spacetime define a traveller by $\theta(\tau)=q\sin(2\pi\tau/T)$ for $0\leq\tau\leq T$, where $q>0$ and $T>0$. Set $t(0)=x(0)=0$ and $dX/d\tau=c(\cosh\theta,\sinh\theta)$. Prove reunion at $x=0$ at rest, find the signed proper acceleration, and prove $T<t(T)\leq T\cosh q$. No closed form for the integral is required. Does nonzero proper acceleration imply curved spacetime?
hintLadder: Proper acceleration in one dimension is $c\,d\theta/d\tau$.
Bound $\cosh(q\sin s)$ and identify where equality with one is possible.
